mainTopic: Combined פיגול intent on an offering and its bread, other versions of רבי אלעזר's question, and רבי מאיר's rule that a זבח makes its נסכים and the מצורע's oil פיגול
overview: Earlier on the daf, רב ruled that if someone slaughters an offering intending to eat a כזית the next day, half from the offering and half from its bread, the bread becomes פיגול but the offering does not. The גמרא asks why we don't use a קל וחומר to keep the bread from becoming פיגול too. It tests this against a ברייתא about seeds planted in another person's vineyard, where the חכמים forbade the seeds but permitted the vines. It then rejects that comparison: the vineyard ruling was only a rabbinic penalty on the wrongdoer, but פיגול is a Torah law. Next the גמרא brings other versions of רבי אלעזר's question. One version is about the two כבשים of שבועות and their שתי הלחם. In it רבי אלעזר explains that his doubt is only about the bread, and the same קל וחומר discussion is repeated. The גמרא also explains how this version relates to the תודה version, based on the waving that ties the כבשים to their bread. A third version, from רבי אבא זוטי, asks whether 'its fellow' means the other lamb or the bread; רב's proof from a משנה is pushed aside. Finally a new משנה teaches, in the name of רבי מאיר, that a זבח can make its נסכים פיגול but not the reverse. The גמרא explains this with ברייתות about נסכים and about the מצורע's לוג of oil. In both, רבא says that רבי מאיר holds they become fixed to the offering at the שחיטה, like the לחמי תודה.

steps.title: The vineyard case: why didn't the חכמים use the קל וחומר there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case where someone planted seeds in another person's vineyard. The חכמים forbade the seeds and permitted the vines, without using the matching קל וחומר. This suggests the קל וחומר is not used here either.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man planted seeds in his friend's vineyard while the grapes were just budding. The case came before the חכמים. They forbade the seeds but permitted the vines. But why? Let us say a קל וחומר: if the thing that makes something else forbidden (the vine) is not itself forbidden, then the seeds, which came to make the vines forbidden but did not succeed, should surely not become forbidden either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a case from a ברייתא and points out that the same kind of קל וחומר would have permitted the seeds. Yet the חכמים still forbade them. That seems to show the קל וחומר is not a good argument for the פיגול case either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, planting seeds in a vineyard (כלאי הכרם) can make both the seeds and the vines forbidden. Here the vines stayed permitted, so by the same logic as our פיגול question the seeds should also be permitted. Since the חכמים forbade them anyway, the גמרא seems to be learning that this kind of קל וחומר is not used.

keyTerms.meaning: The early budding stage of grapes, when the blossoms have just opened
The ban on planting other seeds together with grapevines
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case, or the reverse
The thing that makes something else forbidden
Isn't it logical? (an opening for a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: who planted seeds in his fellow's vineyard when the grapes were budding,
and the incident came before the Sages,
and they forbade the seeds
and they permitted the vines.
But why? Let us say it is a קל וחומר:
If the thing that forbids is not itself forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means the vine, which is what makes the seeds forbidden.

phrases.english: then the thing that came to forbid but did not forbid
phrases.notes: He means the seeds, which could have made the vines forbidden but did not.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that it should not become forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about whether a קל וחומר should stop the bread of the תודה from becoming פיגול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposed קל וחומר that would keep the bread from becoming פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a parallel case the חכמים did not use this קל וחומר. They forbade the seeds even though the vines stayed permitted. So it seems this kind of argument is not used.

steps.title: The vineyard case was only a rabbinic penalty, so פיגול is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. In a vineyard, the Torah forbids only hemp and arum, and other seeds are forbidden only by the רבנן. So forbidding the seeds was a penalty on the wrongdoer. פיגול is a Torah law, so the קל וחומר still applies there.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the Torah only forbids hemp and arum in a vineyard. As the משנה says: if a field was planted with hemp and arum, one may not plant on top of them, because they keep growing for three years. Other seeds are forbidden only by the רבנן. So the person who did wrong (the planter) was penalized by the רבנן, and the person who did nothing wrong (the vineyard owner) was not penalized. But here, by פיגול, let us use the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the vineyard proof. It explains that the vineyard ruling was a penalty (קנס) on the person who sinned, not a matter of logic, so it tells us nothing about פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary seeds in a vineyard are forbidden only by the רבנן. The רבנן chose to penalize only the person who planted wrongly, which is why his seeds were forbidden and the owner's vines were not. פיגול is a Torah law with no penalty factor, so the קל וחומר stands and the question on רב comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Hemp and arum, plants the Torah forbids in a vineyard
By rabbinic law
A penalty the רבנן impose on someone who did wrong
Did a forbidden act

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic penalty (קנס) falls only on the person who sinned, so it cannot teach us about a Torah law like פיגול. In a Torah case, the קל וחומר should apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the challenge on רב's ruling back in place: why should the bread become פיגול when the קל וחומר says it shouldn't?

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There, the Torah forbade only hemp and arum,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הָיְתָה שָׂדֵהוּ זְרוּעָה קַנְבּוֹס וְלוֹף
phrases.english: as we learned: If his field was planted with hemp and arum,
he should not plant on top of them,
because they produce over three years.
Other seeds are forbidden only by rabbinic law.
This one, who did a forbidden act, the Sages penalized,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי דְּלָא עָבֵיד אִיסּוּרָא – לָא קַנְסוּהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: that one, who did not do a forbidden act, the Sages did not penalize.
But here, let us say the קל וחומר!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא? הָתָם קַנְבּוֹס וְלוּף אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the vineyard case that was brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the vineyard case as a proof that the קל וחומר is not used.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vineyard ruling was a rabbinic penalty on the sinner only. It was not a matter of logic, so it does not carry over to the Torah law of פיגול.

steps.title: Another version: רבי אלעזר asked about the lambs of עצרת
steps.stepSummary: Some people teach רבי אלעזר's question as being about the two כבשים brought with the שתי הלחם, not about a תודה. He asked about slaughtering them intending to eat a כזית from them and their bread the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this question about the lambs. רבי אלעזר asked רב: if someone slaughters the lambs intending to eat a כזית, part from them and part from their bread, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי אלעזר's question. It moves the case from the תודה to the two lambs of שבועות that come with the שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is still about intent that mixes the offering and its bread to add up to one כזית. Only the type of offering changes: the כבשים and their loaves instead of the תודה and its bread.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version)
The two lambs brought on שבועות with the שתי הלחם
An olive's worth, the minimum amount for פיגול intent
What is the law?

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it about the lambs,
phrases.notes: "It" means רבי אלעזר's question, which earlier was about the תודה and its bread.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rav:
One who slaughters the lambs
intending to eat an olive-bulk from them and from their bread, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means eating it the next day, after the allowed time, which is what makes it פיגול intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different version of the original question that the earlier discussion was built on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether combined intent, part from the lambs and part from their bread, causes פיגול.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains: his doubt is only about the bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that he has no doubt that the lambs are not פיגול. Even full intent on the bread alone does not make the lambs פיגול. His real question is whether the intent on the lambs combines to make the bread פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: I am not asking whether the lambs become פיגול. If intent to eat a whole כזית of bread does not make the lambs פיגול, then half from them and half from the bread certainly doesn't! My question is about the bread becoming פיגול: does the intent on the lambs join with the intent on the bread to make the bread פיגול, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר narrows down his question. He rules out the lambs and points to the bread as the real subject of his doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that פיגול intent on the bread never makes the lambs פיגול, so half-intent on the bread surely won't. The lambs, however, can make the bread פיגול, so the open question is whether half-intent on the lambs counts together with half-intent on the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by intent to eat it after its allowed time
To become פיגול
Now, if even (opens a "surely" argument)
Do they combine (to add up to the required amount)?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions. Intent on the bread can never make the lambs פיגול, but intent on the lambs can make the bread פיגול. That is why the only question left is about the bread.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's question is only whether the lambs' half of the כזית combines with the bread's half to make the bread פיגול.

phrases.aramaic: לְאִיפַּגּוֹלֵי כְּבָשִׂים לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: About the lambs becoming פיגול I have no question,
now, if when the whole olive-bulk is from the bread they are not פיגול,
is there any question when it is from them and from their bread?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי לְאִיפַּגּוֹלֵי לֶחֶם,
phrases.english: When I asked, it was about the bread becoming פיגול:
do the lambs combine to make the bread פיגול
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאִיפַּגּוֹלֵי כְּבָשִׂים לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows down the question asked in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether intent on the lambs combines with intent on the bread to make the bread פיגול.

steps.title: In the lambs case too, the bread is פיגול and the lambs are not
steps.stepSummary: רב answers רבי אלעזר that here as well, the bread becomes פיגול while the כבשים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even in this case, the bread is פיגול and the lambs are not פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רבי אלעזר's question about the כבשים and the שתי הלחם. The intent combines to make the bread פיגול, but the lambs stay unaffected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר asked only whether the half-intent on the lambs joins with the half-intent on the bread to make the bread פיגול. רב says yes: the bread is פיגול. The lambs stay not פיגול, just as רבי אלעזר already assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: Made פיגול, an offering ruined by a wrong intent about when it will be eaten
The bread, here the שתי הלחם of שבועות
The two lambs brought together with the שתי הלחם

phrases.english: He said to him: Even in this case,
phrases.notes: רב is answering רבי אלעזר. 'This case' is the lambs version of the question.

phrases.english: the bread is rendered פיגול
and the lambs are not rendered פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The intents combine to make the bread פיגול, but the lambs are not פיגול.

steps.title: A קל וחומר says the bread should not be פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling. If the lambs, which help cause the פיגול, are not themselves פיגול, then the bread, which failed to make the lambs פיגול, should surely not become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us say a קל וחומר: if the item that makes something else פיגול does not itself become פיגול, then the item that tried to cause פיגול and failed should surely not become פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's ruling with a קל וחומר. The argument is that the bread should not become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lambs help make the bread פיגול, yet the lambs stay fine. The bread 'tried' to make the lambs פיגול and could not. So the bread is the weaker cause, and it should be even more protected than the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
The thing that causes פיגול, here the lambs
The thing that came to cause פיגול but did not, here the bread

phrases.english: But why? Let us say a קל וחומר:
If the one that renders פיגול is not itself rendered פיגול,
phrases.notes: This means the lambs. Their half-intent helps make the bread פיגול.

phrases.english: then the one that came to render פיגול but did not render it,
phrases.notes: This means the bread. Its half-intent could not make the lambs פיגול.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should not be rendered פיגול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the bread is פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the lambs, which are not פיגול, shows that the bread, the weaker cause, should not be פיגול either.

steps.title: The vineyard case shows this kind of קל וחומר is not used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether such a קל וחומר is valid. In the vineyard case the חכמים forbade the seeds and permitted the vines, even though a matching קל וחומר could have permitted the seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really say a קל וחומר like this? But it was taught: there was a case of someone who planted seeds in his friend's vineyard when the grapes were budding, etc. So why not say a קל וחומר: if the thing that forbids is not itself forbidden, then the thing that came to forbid and did not forbid should surely not be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the קל וחומר itself. It brings the vineyard case, where the חכמים did not use the same kind of reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vineyard, the vines make the seeds forbidden, yet the vines themselves stay permitted. The seeds tried to forbid the vines and failed. By the same קל וחומר the seeds should be permitted, but the חכמים forbade them. This suggests the קל וחומר is not used, which would support רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Grapes at the budding stage
The thing that causes something else to become forbidden
Like this, of this kind

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא?
phrases.english: And do we say a קל וחומר of this kind?
But wasn't it taught: there was an incident with one person

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁזָּרַע כַּרְמוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ סְמָדַר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: who planted seeds in his friend's vineyard while it was budding, etc.
But why? Let them say a קל וחומר:
if the one that forbids is not itself forbidden,
phrases.notes: This means the vines, which make the seeds forbidden.

phrases.english: then the one that came to forbid but did not forbid,
is it not logical that it should not be forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַּוְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר raised in step 6. This repeats the same move made in step 1 for the תודה version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The validity of the קל וחומר from step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים did not apply a matching קל וחומר in the vineyard case, so this type of reasoning may not be used.

steps.title: The vineyard case was a rabbinic penalty, so it proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The Torah forbids only hemp and arum in a vineyard. Other seeds are forbidden only מדרבנן, so the חכמים penalized the wrongdoer and not the innocent owner. פיגול is a Torah law, so the קל וחומר still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the Torah forbade only hemp and arum, and other seeds are forbidden only by the רבנן. The one who did wrong, the רבנן penalized. The one who did no wrong, the רבנן did not penalize. But here, let us say the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the vineyard proof. It explains that the seeds were forbidden as a rabbinic penalty, not through logic about what causes what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding the seeds was a fine on the man who sinned, while the owner of the vines did nothing wrong. That rabbinic reason does not apply to פיגול, which is a Torah law. So the קל וחומר against making the bread פיגול comes back in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Hemp
Arum, a type of plant
By rabbinic law, not Torah law
The רבנן penalized him

steps.whyThisMatters: A rabbinic penalty can single out the wrongdoer without following strict logic. That is why the vineyard case cannot be used to reject a קל וחומר in a Torah law like פיגול.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
There, only hemp and arum did the Torah forbid,
other seeds are forbidden only by the רבנן,
this one, who did a wrong, the רבנן penalized,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא עָבֵד אִיסּוּרָא – לָא קַנְסוּהּ רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: the one who did no wrong, the רבנן did not penalize,
but here, let us say the קל וחומר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the vineyard challenge from step 7. This parallels step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the vineyard comparison. The קל וחומר from step 6 stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vineyard ruling was a rabbinic penalty on the wrongdoer, not a matter of Torah-level logic, so it cannot reject a קל וחומר in a Torah law.

steps.title: How the two versions of רבי אלעזר's question relate
steps.stepSummary: Whoever teaches the question about the תודה would surely apply it to the כבשים too. But whoever teaches it about the כבשים may hold that it applies only there, because the lambs and bread are waved together, unlike the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches it about the תודה would surely apply it to the lambs. But the one who teaches it about the lambs may hold that only the lambs, which are tied to the bread through waving, are included. A תודה, which is not tied to its bread through waving, is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up by comparing the two versions of רבי אלעזר's question. It explains which version includes the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כבשים and the שתי הלחם are waved together, so they are closely linked and their intents may combine. If the question was asked even about a תודה, which has no such link, it surely applies to the כבשים. But asking it about the כבשים does not prove it would be asked about a תודה, because there the intents may obviously not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: The thanks offering, which is brought with loaves
Waving, when the כהן waves the offering
They are bound to each other
All the more so

steps.whatToRemember: The bread can become פיגול through combined intent, but the lambs cannot. The question is more likely to apply to the כבשים than to the תודה, because the כבשים and their bread are waved together.

phrases.english: The one who teaches it about the תודה –
all the more so about the lambs,
but the one who teaches it about the lambs –

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָשִׂים הוּא דְּהוּזְקְקוּ זֶה לָזֶה לִתְנוּפָה,
phrases.english: it is the lambs that are bound to each other through waving,
phrases.notes: The lambs and the שתי הלחם are waved together (ויקרא 23:20).

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תּוֹדָה דְּלֹא הוּזְקְקָה זֶה לָזֶה בִּתְנוּפָה – לָא.
phrases.english: but a תודה, which is not bound to its bread through waving – not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to compare the two versions introduced in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תודה version includes the כבשים version all the more so, but the כבשים version does not necessarily include the תודה, because only the כבשים are waved together with their bread.

steps.title: A third version of רבי אלעזר's question
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אבא זוטי, רבי אלעזר asked רב about someone who slaughters a lamb and intends to eat a כזית 'from its fellow' tomorrow. Does 'its fellow' mean the other lamb or the bread?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא זוטי tells the question this way: רבי אלעזר asked רב, 'If someone slaughters the lamb planning to eat a כזית from its fellow tomorrow, what is the law? Does "its fellow" mean the other lamb, so it does not make it פיגול? Or does it mean the bread, so it does make it פיגול?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי אלעזר's question to רב. This time the question is about what the word 'its fellow' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'its fellow' means the other lamb, there is no פיגול, because one lamb does not make the other lamb פיגול. If it means the bread, then the lamb's slaughter can make the bread פיגול. The whole question depends on what a person usually means by 'its fellow.'

keyTerms.meaning: Asks the question this way (a different version of the question)
Its fellow, its partner, the other one
An olive's size, the smallest amount that counts
It means, it implies
Makes something פיגול

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַבָּא זוּטֵי בָּעֵי לַהּ הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba Zutei asks it this way:
Rabbi Elazar asked of Rav:
One who slaughters the lamb
intending to eat an olive-size from its fellow tomorrow, what is the law?
Does 'its fellow' mean the lamb, so it does not make it piggul,
or perhaps it means 'the bread,' so it makes it piggul?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא זוּטֵי בָּעֵי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי אלעזר's question, now focused on the meaning of the word חבירו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the word חבירו, used by someone slaughtering one of the lambs, mean the other lamb or the bread?

steps.title: רב proves from a משנה that 'its fellow' means the other lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב quotes a משנה. If someone slaughters one lamb to eat from 'its fellow' tomorrow, both lambs are fit. So 'its fellow' must mean the other lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: You already learned it in a משנה. If someone slaughtered one of the lambs planning to eat from it tomorrow, that lamb is פיגול and the other one is fit. If he planned to eat from its fellow tomorrow, both are fit. So we see that 'its fellow' means the lamb!
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers by quoting a משנה. He argues that it shows 'its fellow' means the other lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, planning to eat 'from its fellow' leaves both lambs fit. If 'its fellow' meant the bread, the bread would be פיגול, and the משנה would not say everything is fine. So רב concludes the word means the other lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already (in a משנה)
Fit, valid
So we see, evidently

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
If he slaughtered one of the lambs
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה that comes on the next daf (16a).

phrases.english: intending to eat from it tomorrow,
it is piggul and its fellow is fit.
If he intended to eat from its fellow tomorrow,
both are fit.
So we see that 'its fellow' means the lamb!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 by bringing a proof from a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חבירו means the other lamb, as shown by the משנה where both lambs stay fit.
steps.raayaObject: That חבירו refers to the other lamb.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (16a): שחט אחד מן הכבשים לאכול מחבירו למחר, שניהם כשרים.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about someone who said 'the other lamb' clearly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב's proof. Maybe the משנה is talking about a person who clearly said 'its fellow lamb.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the משנה is talking about someone who spelled it out and said 'its fellow lamb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה may be about a person who made it clear he meant the other lamb. If so, it tells us nothing about someone who only said 'its fellow' without explaining. The question of step 10 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
That he spelled it out, made it clear

steps.whatToRemember: The question of what a plain 'its fellow' means is not settled. The משנה can be read as a case where the person clearly said 'the other lamb.'

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where he spelled it out and said 'its fellow lamb.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be about a person who clearly said 'its fellow lamb,' not just 'its fellow.'

steps.title: The משנה: a זבח can make its נסכים פיגול, but not the other way around
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the זבח makes its נסכים פיגול once they have been made holy in a כלי. The נסכים do not make the זבח פיגול. The משנה gives examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offering makes the נסכים פיגול once they have been made holy in a כלי. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The נסכים do not make the offering פיגול. How so? If someone slaughters the offering planning to eat from it tomorrow, it and its נסכים are פיגול. If he planned to offer its נסכים tomorrow, the נסכים are פיגול but the offering is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that wrong thoughts while slaughtering a זבח can make its נסכים פיגול, but wrong thoughts about the נסכים cannot make the זבח פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נסכים depend on the זבח, so the זבח can pull them into פיגול. But this only applies after the נסכים have been made holy in a כלי. The זבח does not depend on the נסכים, so a wrong thought about the נסכים affects only the נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal offering
The flour, oil and wine that come along with an animal offering
Once they have been made holy in a vessel of the בית המקדש
How so? (introduces examples)
They are פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule works in both directions. The זבח can make the נסכים פיגול, but the נסכים can never make the זבח פיגול.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The offering makes the libations piggul,
once they have been made holy in a vessel,
phrases.notes: Before the נסכים are put into the holy כלי, the זבח cannot make them פיגול.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
The libations do not make the offering piggul.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לֶאֱכוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ לְמָחָר –
phrases.english: One who slaughters the offering intending to eat from it tomorrow:
it and its libations are piggul.
If he intended to offer its libations tomorrow,
the libations are piggul,
the offering is not piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the זבח and its נסכים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a זבח makes its נסכים פיגול once they were made holy in a כלי, but נסכים never make the זבח פיגול.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's reason: the blood permits the נסכים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one is liable for פיגול on the נסכים of an animal, because the blood of the זבח is what permits them to be offered. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: For the נסכים of an animal offering, one is liable because of פיגול, since the blood of the offering permits them to be offered. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains why רבי מאיר holds the נסכים can become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something can become פיגול only if it has a מתיר, something that makes it permitted. רבי מאיר says the blood of the זבח is the מתיר of the נסכים, because it permits them to go on the מזבח. So the נסכים are tied to the זבח and can become פיגול through it.

keyTerms.meaning: The נסכים that come with an animal offering
One is liable (punished)
The blood of the offering
Permits them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the reason behind the משנה. Being permitted by the זבח's blood is what lets the נסכים become פיגול.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
The libations of an animal offering:
one is liable for them because of piggul,
because the blood of the offering permits them to be offered,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִסְכֵי בְּהֵמָה חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר holds that the נסכים of an animal can become פיגול, because the blood of the זבח is what permits them to be offered.

steps.title: The חכמים: נסכים can come ten days later
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר. A person can bring his זבח today and its נסכים up to ten days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי מאיר: But a person can bring his offering today and its נסכים up to ten days later!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבי מאיר's rule from Step 14 that the blood of the זבח is what permits the נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the נסכים can be brought days after the זבח, they clearly don't depend on its blood. So how can the זבח make them פיגול?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so...? (opens a challenge)
his animal offering
and its נסכים (wine, flour and oil offerings that go with it)

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Meir:
But a person may bring his offering today
and its libations up to ten days later!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's ruling in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's claim that the זבח's blood permits the נסכים, so they can become פיגול through it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Things that can be brought separately, days later, are not dependent on the זבח.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only נסכים brought together with the זבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that he only meant נסכים that come together with the זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only said it about נסכים that come together with the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר narrows his rule so the challenge no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that נסכים brought on a later day are separate. His rule covers only נסכים brought along with the זבח. Those are tied to it and can become פיגול through it.

keyTerms.meaning: I too only said... (narrowing one's own statement)
those that come together with the offering

phrases.english: He said to them:
I too did not say it
except about those that come with the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's rule seemed to cover all נסכים, even ones brought days later.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers נסכים brought together with the זבח.

steps.title: The חכמים: the נסכים could be moved to another זבח
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים push back. Even נסכים brought with this זבח could still be switched to a different זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It is possible to switch them to another offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר's narrowed answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the נסכים can still be used for a different זבח, they are not really bound to this one. So this זבח should not make them פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: it is possible
to switch it (to a different use)
another offering

phrases.english: They said to him:
It is possible to switch it to another offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's answer in Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נסכים brought with the זבח are tied to it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that can be moved to another offering is not bound to this one.

steps.title: רבא: they become fixed at the שחיטה, like the לחמי תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי מאיר holds the נסכים become fixed to the זבח at the שחיטה, like the loaves of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי מאיר holds they become fixed at the slaughter, like the loaves of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how רבי מאיר would answer the last challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the שחיטה, the נסכים could be switched to another זבח. Once the animal is slaughtered, they are locked to this זבח. So intent during the שחיטה makes them פיגול, just as with the לחמי תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (this is his view)
they became fixed / locked in
slaughter of the animal
the loaves brought with a thanks offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, the שחיטה locks the accompanying items to the זבח, like the לחמי תודה. That is why they can become פיגול through it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Meir holds
they became fixed at the slaughter,
like the loaves of a thanks offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17 on behalf of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the נסכים can be switched, they seem not to be bound to this זבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: They can be switched only until the שחיטה. After that they are fixed to this זבח.

steps.title: The לוג of oil of a מצורע can become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one is liable for פיגול on the לוג of oil of a מצורע, because the blood of the אשם permits the oil to be put on the thumbs and toes. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One is liable for פיגול on the לוג of oil of a מצורע, because the blood of the אשם permits it for the thumbs and toes. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא about the מצורע's oil and his אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the נסכים. The oil depends on the blood of the אשם, since only after that blood may the oil be put on the מצורע's thumb and big toe. So for רבי מאיר, an אשם that became פיגול makes the oil פיגול too.

keyTerms.meaning: a לוג (a measure) of oil
a person with צרעת who brings offerings to become pure
guilt offering
permits it
the right thumb and big toe

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The log of oil of a leper,
one is liable for it because of piggul,
because the blood of the guilt offering
permits it for the thumbs and toes,
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 14. Some of the oil goes on the מצורע's right thumb and big toe, after the אשם's blood.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לוֹג שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the נסכים discussion in Steps 14-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי מאיר, the מצורע's לוג of oil becomes פיגול through his אשם, because the אשם's blood permits the oil.

steps.title: The חכמים: the לוג can come ten days later
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי מאיר. A person can bring his אשם today and his לוג up to ten days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי מאיר: But a person can bring his אשם today and his לוג from now up to ten days later!
steps.whatsHappening: The same first challenge as Step 15, now about the מצורע's oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oil can be brought days after the אשם, it seems separate from it. Then the אשם should not make the oil פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: his guilt offering
his לוג of oil
from now until

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Meir:
But a person may bring his guilt offering today,
and his log from now until ten days later.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר: וַהֲלֹא אָדָם מֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's claim that the אשם's blood makes the oil dependent on it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Oil that can be brought days later is not tied to the אשם.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: only a לוג brought with the אשם
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that he only meant a לוג brought together with the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I too only said it about a לוג that comes together with the אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר narrows his rule, just as in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil brought on a later day is separate. Only oil brought along with the אשם is tied to it.

keyTerms.meaning: one that comes together with the guilt offering

phrases.english: He said to them:
I too did not say it
except about one that comes with the guilt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְּבָא עִם הָאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to cover any לוג, even one brought later.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a לוג brought with the אשם.

steps.title: The oil could be moved to another אשם
steps.stepSummary: The challenge returns. The oil could still be switched to a different אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to switch it to another אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge again, just as in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oil can still be used for another אשם, it is not bound to this one. So this אשם should not make it פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: another guilt offering

phrases.english: It is possible to switch it to another guilt offering.
phrases.notes: The text doesn't say "they said to him" here, but it's still the חכמים pushing back, like in Step 17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's answer in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a לוג brought with the אשם is tied to it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something that can be moved to another offering is not bound to this one.

steps.title: רבא: the oil is fixed at the שחיטה, like the לחמי תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the same answer. רבי מאיר holds the oil becomes fixed to the אשם at its שחיטה, like the loaves of a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי מאיר holds they become fixed at the slaughter, like the loaves of a תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the last challenge with the same idea he used for the נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the אשם is slaughtered, the oil could go to another אשם. After the שחיטה, it is locked to this אשם. So it can become פיגול through it.

keyTerms.meaning: like, just as (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: The same principle covers both נסכים and the מצורע's oil. For רבי מאיר, the שחיטה locks them to their offering, like the לחמי תודה, so the offering can make them פיגול.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Meir holds
they became fixed at the slaughter,
like the loaves of a thanks offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: קָסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּקְבְּעוּ בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 with the same principle as Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the oil can be switched, it seems not to be bound to this אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the שחיטה, the oil is fixed to this אשם, like the לחמי תודה.
